summary: Mobile heading-colour parity verification (iter376). Core fix for AppHeader title + T component default (heading-font → colors.heading) is WORKING: Dashboard greeting, AI Tools heading, and Reports hero all render brand TEAL rgb(14,77,82) in light and WHITE rgb(255,255,255) in dark. Drawer label reads exactly 'Sign Out' and 'drawer-caring-for' card is present. HOWEVER — the fix is incomplete: many screens still pass an explicit `color: colors.text` on heading-font <T> elements, which overrides the new default and makes those section titles render in near-black (#1C2B2D) in LIGHT mode. The PRD specifically called out that Reports 'Generate a Report' + 'Your reports' section titles must be teal — they are NOT. Dark mode happens to mask the bug because colors.text == colors.heading == #FFFFFF in dark. No invisible-on-solid-colour regressions found (tool cards still use explicit #FFFFFF on coloured tiles — OK). No red-screen errors; tabs navigate fine.

action_items: Sweep /app/mobile/app and /app/mobile/src for the pattern `fontFamily: fonts.heading` (or fonts.headingSemi) combined with `color: colors.text` and either (a) remove the explicit color so T's new default (colors.heading) applies, or (b) replace with `color: colors.heading`. Keep explicit white/primaryFg on heading-text that sits on solid teal/clay/sage backgrounds (ai-tools tool cards at ai-tools.tsx:140 are already correct).

Also fix: plan-billing.tsx:71, chsp-tools.tsx (8 spots), price-history.tsx (5 spots), plan-select.tsx (3 spots), documents.tsx:332, athm.tsx:111, athm-project/[id].tsx:123, complaints.tsx:275, provider-switch.tsx:182, provider-quality/[name].tsx:161, about.tsx:232, statement-compare/[id].tsx:101/105, switch-decision/[sid].tsx:92, report/[id].tsx:49.
Decide product intent for report card titles (reports.tsx:114) — if teal is wanted, promote to heading-font + colors.heading; otherwise leave as body.
critical_code_review_comments: The T component now defaults heading-font text to colors.heading, which is the right systemic fix — but the migration is only half-done: ~25+ explicit `color: colors.text` overrides on heading-font <T> instances remain across the mobile code and silently defeat the fix in light mode. The bug is masked in dark mode only because colors.text and colors.heading both equal #FFFFFF there.

Suggest adding an ESLint rule or codemod check: a <T> whose style sets fontFamily to fonts.heading/headingSemi should not also set an explicit color unless it is colors.primaryFg or '#FFFFFF' (for on-solid-colour cases).

success_rate.frontend: partial — core T/AppHeader fix works, but ~15 screens still show non-teal headings in light

context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent sweeps the explicit `color: colors.text` overrides on heading-font <T>s, re-test by (1) logging in as cathy@example.com / testpass123 at the mobile Expo preview, (2) visiting /reports, /chsp-tools, /price-history, /plan-select, /plan-billing in LIGHT mode and asserting the colour of each section heading is rgb(14,77,82) via `getComputedStyle(el).color`, (3) toggling to DARK and asserting rgb(255,255,255). Drawer 'Sign Out' label and theme-dark toggle are confirmed working — no need to retest.
rca of the issue: Main agent added `colors.heading` to tokens.ts and made the T component default heading-font text to `colors.heading`, and set AppHeader title to `colors.heading` — that part of the fix is correct and verified on Dashboard (dashboard-greeting), Tools (ai-tools-heading) and Reports hero. However existing screens (reports.tsx, chsp-tools.tsx, price-history.tsx, plan-select.tsx, plan-billing.tsx, documents.tsx, about.tsx, complaints.tsx, athm*.tsx, provider-switch/quality, statement-compare, switch-decision, report/[id]) all explicitly pass `color: colors.text` on their heading-font <T> elements. Because an explicit style wins over the component's default, those section headings continue to render in colors.text (#1C2B2D in light) instead of the new colors.heading teal. Dark mode hides the bug because both tokens are #FFFFFF in dark. Mitigation: either delete the explicit `color: colors.text` on heading-font <T> instances (so the default applies) or change it to `colors.heading`.
